faqs.question: Do you take walk-in tattoos in downtown Macon?
faqs.answer: Yes. Walk-ins are welcome Tuesday through Saturday whenever an artist chair is open. Smaller flash pieces, script, and straightforward designs are often taken the same day. For larger custom work, sleeves, or cover-ups that require custom drawing time, book a consultation or call (478) 259-1829 before heading down to 484 Cherry St.

faqs.question: What are Tooth & Nail Tattoo Parlour's hours?
faqs.answer: Tooth & Nail is open five days a week at 484 Cherry St in downtown Macon, GA: Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday from 1:00 PM to 8:00 PM, and Friday and Saturday from 1:00 PM to 10:00 PM. The parlour is closed on Sunday and Monday.

faqs.question: Where are you located and where do I park on Cherry Street?
faqs.answer: We are located at 484 Cherry St, Macon, GA 31201, right in the heart of downtown Macon near the Cherry Street dining and retail corridor and a short drive from Mercer University. Street parking is available along Cherry Street and adjacent downtown blocks.

faqs.question: How much does a tattoo cost?
faqs.answer: Pricing depends on final size, placement on the body, level of detail, color saturation, and artist time—so we do not quote flat prices blindly over social media or phone without reviewing your idea. Call (478) 259-1829, submit a consultation request online, or stop by the shop for an accurate estimate.

faqs.question: Do I need to put down a deposit to book a custom appointment?
faqs.answer: Custom appointments and multi-hour sessions require a deposit confirmed directly with your chosen artist or the shop desk (for example, several resident artists take a $50 booking deposit applied toward the tattoo). Always confirm your artist's exact deposit policy and accepted payment method directly—never send money to unverified accounts.

faqs.question: What is the minimum age and ID requirement?
faqs.answer: Plan on being 18 years of age or older with a valid, unexpired government-issued photo ID (such as a driver's license, state ID, or passport) for any tattoo or piercing service. If you have questions regarding identification or age rules, call (478) 259-1829 before arriving.

faqs.question: Do you offer body piercings?
faqs.answer: Yes—resident professional body piercer Tyler (@hol3_punch3r) performs sterile body piercings, facial piercings, and curated ear styling at Tooth & Nail Wednesday through Saturday (walk-ins and appointments). Call (478) 259-1829 or message @hol3_punch3r to check same-day availability and jewelry options.

faqs.question: Is Tooth & Nail licensed and inspected by the health department?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tooth & Nail Tattoo Parlour operates under licensing from the Macon-Bibb County Board of Health (171 Emory Highway, Macon, GA; phone (478) 745-0411) and has served Cherry Street and Middle Georgia for more than a decade with strict single-use needle and sterilization protocols.

faqs.question: Does getting a tattoo or piercing hurt?
faqs.answer: Yes—both tattooing and piercing involve discomfort, though tolerance varies widely by person and placement. Spots over bone or thin skin (ribs, feet, hands, sternum) feel sharper than fleshier areas like the outer arm or calf. Eat a solid meal beforehand, hydrate well, and ask your artist what to expect for your chosen placement.

faqs.question: Can I go swimming or take a bath with a new tattoo?
faqs.answer: No. Do not submerge a fresh tattoo in pools, lakes, rivers, oceans, hot tubs, or bathtubs for at least 3 weeks while the skin seals and heals. Soaking softens healing skin and sharply raises infection risk. Brief, clean showers are fine—if you have a beach trip coming up, schedule your tattoo for after you get home.

faqs.question: Why does my new tattoo look like ink is leaking out under the wrap?
faqs.answer: Your tattoo is not fading or rejecting ink. During the first few days, your body produces plasma and lymph fluid to heal the skin, which naturally mixes with excess surface pigment to form a dark, cloudy liquid under Soku or second-skin wraps. Follow the wash and moisturizing steps on our Aftercare page and check with your artist if anything looks unusual.

soku.title: Routine 01: Soku Second-Skin Wrap
soku.summary: Follow these six steps if your artist sealed your fresh tattoo with Soku Tattoo Aftercare film.

steps.name: Keep the wrap on for 3 to 7 days
steps.text: Leave Soku Tattoo Aftercare on the tattoo for at least 3 days. You may leave the protective film on up to a full week as long as the seal remains intact and the skin is not irritated.

steps.name: Expect dark fluid underneath
steps.text: During the first few days, plasma, blood, and excess surface ink will pool as a dark, cloudy liquid inside the pocket. This is completely normal and protects the healing tattoo.

steps.name: Remove gently in a warm shower
steps.text: After at least 3 days, peel the wrap off slowly in the shower using warm water and Dial Gold antibacterial soap. Lift a corner carefully until soap and water break the adhesive seal without pulling on the skin.

steps.name: Wash morning and night for 2 days
steps.text: For the next two days after removing the film, gently wash the tattoo with Dial Gold morning and night. Pat completely dry with a clean disposable paper towel—never rub with a cloth bath towel.

steps.name: Moisturize lightly starting day 3
steps.text: On the third day after film removal, apply a thin layer of unscented, dye-free lotion if the skin feels dry or tight. Shop-recommended options include Lubriderm, Jergens, Cornhuskers, Curel, or Eucerin.

steps.name: Remove early if the seal leaks
steps.text: If fluid leaks out from an edge before day 3, bacteria can get in. Remove the wrap immediately in the shower and transition straight to the traditional wash-and-lotion routine below.

traditional.title: Routine 02: Standard Bandage & Ointment
traditional.summary: Follow these eight steps if your artist sent you home with a traditional wrap or absorbent pad.

steps.name: First wash when you get home
steps.text: Leave the shop bandage on until you arrive home. Remove it cleanly, wash gently with Dial Gold antibacterial soap, and pat dry with a clean paper towel. Wash once more at bedtime; if you have pets, you may cover it loosely with clean cling wrap on the first night only once completely dry.

steps.name: Wash twice daily for days 1 to 4
steps.text: For the first 3 to 4 days, wash your tattoo with Dial Gold morning and night—and any time you sweat heavily or get dirty—then pat dry with a fresh paper towel.

steps.name: Apply a whisper-thin layer of Aquaphor
steps.text: During days 1 to 4, rub in a very thin sheen of Aquaphor or an artist-approved ointment. Applying too much ointment traps moisture, suffocates pores, and causes heavy scabbing or weeping.

steps.name: Switch to unscented lotion around day 5
steps.text: Around day 5, swap ointment for a small amount of fragrance-free, dye-free lotion (Lubriderm, Jergens, Cornhuskers, Curel, or Eucerin) as needed for about two weeks until peeling settles.

steps.name: Know what normal healing feels like
steps.text: Mild redness, warmth, itching, light flaking, and slight swelling are normal parts of the healing cycle. Never scratch or pick peeling flakes—pat gently or apply a light dot of lotion.

steps.name: Keep scented soaps off in the shower
steps.text: Quick showers are fine, but keep harsh body washes, scrubs, and shampoo away from the fresh tattoo. If soap runs over it, rinse and wash gently with Dial Gold at the end of your shower.

steps.name: No soaking or swimming for 2 to 3 weeks
steps.text: Avoid pools, lakes, oceans, hot tubs, and soaking in bathtubs for at least 2 to 3 weeks until the surface skin is fully healed.

steps.name: Protect fresh ink from direct sun
steps.text: Keep a healing tattoo covered from direct sunlight and tanning beds. Once fully healed, daily broad-spectrum sunscreen keeps lines sharp and colors bright for years.
